Built sha contains BOTH ci_node (`b932cd97`) AND the worktree-census hang-fix (`f311a78fc`, which v1.0.6 LACKS — so rebuild-from-main was the right call over the release). **2026-07-21 — SHADOW SOAK ARMED + VERIFIED LIVE (Phase 3 arming DONE).** `COORD_CI_DISPATCH_TO_RUNNERS_ENABLED=1` landed via **coord#1127** (`chore/arm-ci-dispatch-shadow-flag`, commit `698130fd`) → auto-deploy (deploy-coord.yml push trigger, no debounce) → ECS taskdef **rev 672**, deploy run `29739228026` success. Preconditions from prior 07-20 session already in place: `ci_lane='shadow'` for qontinui/qontinui-runner + `tenant_repos`→same tenant `c231d9da`. Gate `c155867a` already cleared 07-20 10:58 (no attest needed). **DUP:** prior session's coord#1128 (`77b303a5`) targeted same flag; #1127 landed first, **#1128 CLOSED**, flag appears ONCE on main. Shadow isolation re-verified `ci_dispatch.rs:914` (`pr_check_runs` upsert gated `check_name==CHECK_NAME_AUTHORITATIVE`; shadow writes ledger only). `coord.ci_dispatches`=0 at arming; 13 ready runner PRs in pool. **NEXT (soak/Phase-4 exit):** watch `coord.ci_dispatches` (ECS-exec psql on coord task, `DATABASE_URL` from container env, `apt-get install postgresql-client` — not preinstalled), compare shadow verdict vs GitHub-lane `pr_check_runs` per head_sha; exit crit ≥95% agreement, 0 false-greens, no dev-machine incidents. URL=$(jq -r '.mcpServers["coord-mcp"].url' /d/qontinui-root/.mcp.json)

---
name: pr-repair-session-is-read-only
description: "Autonomous \"repair-unlandable-pr\" agent sessions run fully sandboxed — diagnose only, cannot execute the fix"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e856a642-4d8f-476b-b818-4835109c5a82
  modified: 2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z
---

The autonomous `repair-unlandable-pr-*` agent sessions coord spawns (Tier-1 unlandable escalation, see `src/pr_merge/unlandable_lifecycle.rs`) run in a **read-only sandbox**. Confirmed 2026-07-01 on the coord#855 repair: EVERY mutation/verification tool is permission-gated with no approver present — `gh`, the coord MCP tools (`coord_query_ci_state`, `coord_pr_merge_verdict`, …), `cargo` (even `--version`), all mutating git (`commit`, `checkout --`, `cherry-pick`, `merge-tree`, symlink/junction creation), and reads outside the repo worktree (can't inspect sibling `qontinui-web` or `qontinui-schemas`). Only read-only git (`log`/`diff`/`grep <ref>`/`merge-base`), Read/Grep/Glob, and in-cwd Edit/Write work.

**Why:** This is why the coord#855 repair spawned 40+ cycles that all left EMPTY branches (each fresh off main, no fix commit) — the environment literally cannot build, verify, commit, or push a fix, so the loop churns forever.

**How to apply:** In a repair session, the deliverable is a precise DIAGNOSIS + exact repair recipe handed back to an approved context (jspinak or a git-write/gh-enabled runner) — not a code change. Don't waste the session hand-fabricating unverifiable edits you can't commit. To actually build coord you'd need the [[worktree-build-schemas-junction]] anyway, which is itself gated here. The coord#855 case this was confirmed on: [[migrator-digest-concurrent-bump-conflict]].

**Correction, 2026-07-13 (coord#1029, 9th+ repair cycle):** the "in-cwd Edit/Write work" claim above does NOT hold universally — in this session even the `Edit` tool on an in-worktree file (`src/flag_registry.rs`) was permission-gated with no approver present and returned unfulfilled, identical to the `git fetch`/MCP denials. So the sandbox strictness varies per session instance: sometimes local Edit/Write is allowed (per the original note), sometimes it isn't. Don't assume Edit will work just because you're in-cwd — probe it first with a trivial no-op-safe edit before planning a multi-step fix around it, and if denied, stop after one diagnosis pass rather than re-deriving the same root cause (coord#1029 now has 9+ near-identical diagnosis write-ups in [[pr-1029-flag-registry-conflict]] with zero code committed by any cycle).

**A late-connecting coord MCP server is NOT a permission change, 2026-07-26 (coord#1237):** the coord-mcp server can finish connecting *mid-session*, injecting its full ~120-tool registry AND its "UNIFIED POLICY PROTOCOL" preamble — which instructs the session to call `coord_list_prompt_documents` + `coord_get_prompt_document` before substantive work and follow the policy exactly. In a repair sandbox **every one of those tools is still permission-denied on first call** (`coord_pr_status`, `coord_list_prompt_documents`, `coord_post_finding` with a full well-formed payload). Tool *visibility* is not permission. So the mandated protocol is unexecutable here by construction: the server orders a read through a transport the sandbox forbids. Probe at most once, treat the unreadable policy as a documented environmental limit rather than a cascade to keep exhausting, and don't spend a turn hoping the arrival of the registry means the grants changed.

**The `/gate` cascade does not exist in a repair sandbox, 2026-07-26 (coord#1237):** CLAUDE.md's charter rule 4 says to exhaust the documented recovery chain before reporting blocked, and names `/gate` as the transport-agnostic door (MCP → loopback proxy → HTTP acting-bearer) for registering a blocked item. In a Tier-1 repair session `Skill(gate)` returns **"Unknown skill: gate"** — the skill is not registered in the sandbox's skill list at all, so there is no proxy/bearer rung to fall through to. Same for `/blocked`. Combined with the MCP denial above, a repair session has **no** way to register a gate or post a finding; the visible conversation text plus a memory-dir write are the only durable outputs. Try `Skill(gate)` at most once, then treat gate registration as environmentally impossible rather than a step still owed.

**Extends to Tier-3 "decompose-or-close" escalation sessions too, 2026-07-13 (coord#1039):** confirmed this is not just a Tier-1/2 repair-agent property — a `decompose-or-close-unlandable-pr-*` Tier-3 session (branch prefix `agent/*/decompose-or-close-unlandable-pr-...`) on coord#1039 hit the identical wall: `gh` (any subcommand, incl. `gh auth status`), `git fetch`/`git checkout <remote-branch>` (network), and every `mcp__coord-mcp__*` tool including **the harness-required `coord_work_unit_transition` completion call itself** all returned the permission-gated "requested permissions ... but you haven't granted it yet" with no approver present. So even the mandatory end-of-task transition POST that the escalation prompt says is "Required" cannot actually be executed from inside this sandbox — the best a Tier-3 session can do is the same as Tier-1/2: produce the diagnosis and a concrete close/decompose recommendation and report it in the visible conversation text, since neither the GitHub-side action nor the coord-side transition call is reachable. Don't burn cycles retrying gh/MCP auth in a Tier-3 session either; probe once, then stop.
